title: Still Learning
logline: In a mask-carving workshop on the south-west coast, apprentices at every stage work beside a carver who has done it for decades, and who still calls themselves a learner.

object.note: Object 4 (identity not chosen) may appear subtly, for example among Chathura's things while he travels, waits or watches, only where it sits naturally in a real moment. Never staged, never the subject.

thread_in.thread: Different temperaments in one kitchen become different stages in one workshop: apprentices at every level beside a carver who still calls themselves a learner.

thread_out.thread: If even the master is still learning, the way out of the fog is not certainty; in the high hills the fog is literal, and the only way through is to slow down and look.

lesson.in_simple_terms: Even someone who has practised for decades can honestly call themselves a learner. The texts use that very word for everyone on the path until its very end, and say the restless, unsettled mind is among the last things to fall away.
lesson.in_simple_terms_si: දශක ගණනක් පුරුදු වූ කෙනාත් අවංකවම තවම ඉගෙන ගන්නෙකි; මාර්ගයේ අවසානයට පැමිණෙන තුරු හැමෝම 'හික්මෙන' අය බව ධර්මය කියයි.
lesson.the_teaching: The Abhidhamma counts eight noble persons, at the path and fruit of four stages, and calls all but the last a learner (sekha), one still in training; only the final stage is 'beyond learning' (asekha). Pradeepika shows specific states stopping in a fixed order: doubt no longer arises after stream-entry, hatred only after non-return, while the restless mind remains until the very end. A good guide, the texts on temperament add, does not give everyone the same instruction but looks closely at each student, or asks.
lesson.how_the_film_shows_it: Hands at every level of skill work on the same kind of face, and the camera stays with an apprentice's mistake and the master's small correction. Harder faces are handed over slowly, one person at a time, according to what the master sees in each. When the master still calls themselves a learner, the viewer feels how long it takes to see what an expert sees, and that the learning does not stop.

key_terms.en: learner, one still in training / one beyond training
good friend; spiritual guide or teacher

lesson.caution: The stages in the texts are spiritual, not craft skill, and they are not badges to display: the workshop only makes visible what it means to still be learning.
lesson.builds_on: The almsgiving showed that people lose their way differently; the workshop shows that finding it is also gradual, guided person by person, with no one quite finished.
lesson.evidence_class: editorial interpretation grounded in cited source teaching
